title: Torsion cohomological dimension of a separably closed field
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field. Then
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq0$ in the sense of
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]: for every
torsion étale sheaf $F$ on
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ and every $q>0$ one has
$H^q(\operatorname{Spec}K,F)=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-separably-closed-sections-preserve-epi] to terminal sections on Spec K. Transfer preservation of epimorphisms to Sheaf.Γ along Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections, using isTerminalEtalePoint.

Global sections is additive and is a right adjoint, so it preserves kernels. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels gives preservation of homology, and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology gives exactness. The proved source-library comparison Functor.singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso identifies RΓ applied to F in degree zero with Γ(F) in degree zero.

Unfold [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Apply the degree-q homology functor to the comparison in step 2. For q>0, DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE shows that the target is zero, since a degree-zero single object is IsLE 0. Transport zero across the homology isomorphism and use AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton. Since this works for every abelian sheaf, it implies the torsion bound [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].
